version.changelog:
- Initial release of yunlv-pod-agent, focused on AI-powered automation for Print on Demand (POD) business operations.
- Provides step-by-step guidance on building and optimizing POD workflows with AI Agents, including product design, store management, and customer service.
- Includes tiered tool recommendations and workflow schemes for beginners, advanced users, and large-scale store operations.
- Offers best practices for safe AI-generated design, copyright compliance, and data privacy.
- Integrates references such as tool comparison tables, design formulas, and operational checklists for practical application.
- Supports integration with Yunlv AI TradeGPT API and other user-configured platform APIs.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: yunlv-pod-agent
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle is a comprehensive instructional guide for automating Print-on-Demand (POD) businesses using AI agents. It contains no executable code, focusing instead on metadata (SKILL.md, clawhub.yaml) and reference documentation. It demonstrates good security posture by explicitly defining permission boundaries that forbid unauthorized API operations and data sharing, while providing clear guidance on copyright safety and data privacy.

llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (POD automation) generally matches the APIs and instructions, but there is an internal metadata inconsistency about required credentials and the skill expects API keys (TRADEGPT_API_KEY and user platform API) that you should verify and limit before trusting.

dimensions.detail: The skill is an instruction-only POD automation/consulting agent and declares use of a YunlvAI TradeGPT API (api.yunlvai.com) and a user-configured Platform API for store operations — these are coherent with the POD automation purpose. However, the registry summary at the top of the package metadata lists "Required env vars: none" while both SKILL.md and clawhub.yaml declare TRADEGPT_API_KEY as required/primaryEnv. This mismatch is an inconsistency that should be clarified by the publisher.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md contains prose guidance, templates, and references for building POD agents. It does not contain instructions to read arbitrary system files, harvest unrelated credentials, or post data to unexpected endpoints. It does refer to configuring API keys for the TradeGPT API and user platform APIs, which is expected for store automation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files, so nothing is downloaded or written to disk by an installer. That is the lowest-risk install mechanism.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares TRADEGPT_API_KEY as the primary credential and references a user-configurable Platform API for store operations. Requesting an API key for the service it uses is proportionate, but you should be cautious: platform-store API keys grant the ability to perform actions (listings, refunds, etc.). The earlier top-level metadata omission of required env vars increases risk of user confusion about what credentials will actually be requested or used.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled (always:false) and does not request system-wide privileges or modify other skills. It relies on external APIs and user-supplied platform credentials; autonomous invocation is allowed by default but that is normal for skills.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says (POD automation) and legitimately needs an API key for YunlvAI's TradeGPT and optional store platform credentials to act on your shop. Before installing: 1) Confirm whether the platform will actually prompt you for TRADEGPT_API_KEY (clawhub.yaml and SKILL.md require it) — ask the publisher why the top-level registry summary omitted it. 2) Verify the API host (https://api.yunlvai.com) and the publisher (yunlvai.com) are trustworthy for your use case. 3) Provide the minimum necessary platform permissions (avoid giving full admin keys; create scoped API tokens if possible). 4) Test with a sandbox/store account and limit exposure of real customer data until you trust the agent's behavior. 5) If you need higher assurance, ask the publisher for a clear privacy/data-retention policy and for details on what TradeGPT does with your shop data. If you cannot verify these points, proceed cautiously or avoid providing store API credentials.
